title: Git Rebasing
description: Learn how to rewrite history and maintain a clean project timeline using git rebase

steps.title: Understanding Rebase
steps.content:
Rebase rewrites commit history:

Key concepts:
- Moving commits to new base
- Linear history vs. merge commits
- Rewriting public history risks
- Interactive rebasing

Differences from merge:
- Merge: Preserves history
- Rebase: Creates linear history
- Merge: Safe for public branches
- Rebase: Best for local branches

steps.title: Basic Rebasing
steps.content:
Rebase your branch onto latest main:

Steps:
1. git checkout feature-branch
2. git rebase main
3. Resolve any conflicts
4. git push --force-with-lease (if needed)

Common scenarios:
- Update feature branch
- Clean up local history
- Incorporate upstream changes

Warning: Never rebase public/shared branches!

practical_task.description: Create a feature branch, make changes, then rebase it onto main. Type 'done' when complete.

steps.title: Interactive Rebasing
steps.content:
Modify commit history interactively:

Command: git rebase -i <commit>

Options:
- pick: Keep commit as-is
- reword: Change message
- edit: Amend commit
- squash: Combine with previous
- fixup: Combine and discard message
- drop: Remove commit

Common uses:
- Squash related commits
- Fix commit messages
- Remove unnecessary commits
- Split large commits

practical_task.description: Use interactive rebase to squash your last two commits. What command starts interactive rebase?

steps.title: Handling Rebase Conflicts
steps.content:
Resolve conflicts during rebase:

When conflicts occur:
1. Fix conflicts in files
2. git add resolved files
3. git rebase --continue

Other options:
- git rebase --abort: Cancel rebase
- git rebase --skip: Skip current commit

Best practices:
- Small, focused commits
- Regular rebasing
- Clear commit messages
- Backup branches

practical_task.description: Create and resolve a rebase conflict. Type 'done' when resolved.

exercises.question: What is the main difference between merge and rebase?
exercises.explanation: Rebase creates a linear history by moving commits to a new base, while merge preserves the branch history with a merge commit.

exercises.question: What command starts an interactive rebase?
exercises.explanation: git rebase -i <commit> starts an interactive rebase session where you can modify commits.

exercises.question: What command continues a rebase after resolving conflicts?
exercises.explanation: After resolving conflicts, use git rebase --continue to proceed with the rebase operation.

exercises.question: What flag safely force pushes after rebase?
exercises.explanation: git push --force-with-lease is safer than --force as it checks if the remote branch has been updated.
